stories.title: OpenAI Withdraws 3 Math Papers
stories.reason: OpenAI withdrew 3 of its math.github.io research claims after a sign error invalidated a trace-cancellation argument; the retraction + mass proof-repair update is the week's biggest verifiability story and directly tests whether AI-generated math can be trusted unverified.
key_facts: 3 withdrawn: 'Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds', 'Algebraicity of Kuga-Satake Correspondences for K3 Surfaces', 'The rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces'
Cause: a sign error in the first paper invalidated a stabilization-trace cancellation argument used by the two dependent papers
Same update: 14 manuscripts got proof repairs/corrected statements, 13 more cite revised companion papers, formalized top-line results now 300/719 (~42%)
History entry dated 2026-10-07

stories.title: OpenAI annualised revenues $20B less than previously signalled
stories.reason: CNBC and FT both report OpenAI's annualized revenue run-rate is ~$20B below what was previously signalled to investors/partners (Nvidia, Oracle, CoreWeave deals in context) — a concrete, two-source-confirmed data point in the AI-spending-bubble debate that working engineers and investors both need to know.
key_facts: Two independent outlets (FT, CNBC) ran the same $20B shortfall figure the same day
Context ties to OpenAI's Nvidia/Oracle/CoreWeave compute commitments

stories.title: “Math 2.0” will need to value mathematical progress more holistically
stories.reason: Terence Tao's widely-discussed (589 pts/625 comments, the single highest-engagement item in today's pool) post argues math needs a 'Math 2.0' evaluation framework that values progress more holistically — landing the same week AI-generated proofs had to be partially retracted. Directly on-topic for the always-surface 'evaluation methodology' beat. Could not fetch mathstodon.xyz (blocked) to quote him directly, so this is scored on title + context, not text.
key_facts: Posted 2026-10-08, same week as the OpenAI math-paper withdrawal (133541a06ad0)
589 points / 625 comments on HN — the highest engagement of any candidate today

stories.title: Port of the TypeScript compiler, checker and lsp to Rust, by LLM
stories.reason: A solo dev used Claude Opus 5.5 (after an earlier GPT-5.6/GPT-6 attempt cost $400k+) to port the entire TypeScript 7 compiler/checker/LSP to Rust: a working v0 in ~10 hours for ~$24k, passing all 181,711 ported Go tests, with tsc-rs running ~1.6x faster than tsc 7 and up to ~11x faster than tsc 6 on real repos. Concrete evidence of what frontier agentic coding can now do unsupervised on a huge, well-specified codebase.
key_facts: GPT-5.6 Sol/GPT-6 Astra: 1.3M lines of Rust, months of work, 84% compat, $400k+ in tokens
Claude Opus 5.5: working v0 in ~10 hours, ~$24,047 over two weeks (~925-983% of a $200 plan's weekly limit)
All 181,711 ported Go tests pass; TanStack Query and Hono diagnostics are identical to Go's
Geometric-mean speedup over tsc 6 across 6 real apps: 7.1x (tsc7), 11.4x (tsc-rs), 20.9x (bun check)
Author: 'never read a line of this code'; editor features (hover, refactors) not ported yet

stories.title: Whistle: Speech to Text in 16.9 MB
stories.reason: A speech-to-text model that fits in 16.9 MB hit #1 on HN (504 pts) — exactly the kind of serving/footprint efficiency story the taste profile always wants, though cactuscompute.com is blocked so this is scored on the HN title/engagement alone, not the blog's own benchmark numbers.
key_facts: 16.9 MB total model size (claimed in title)
504 points / 115 comments on HN

stories.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
stories.reason: RoboJEPA (Meta/FAIR's JEPA team, incl. Assran and Ballas) establishes the first scaling law for multi-embodiment robotic world models trained on real robot data, and ships model checkpoints plus training/deployment code — the repo-attached exception to 'arxiv alone doesn't count.'
key_facts: 8B parameters — described as the largest JEPA predictor model trained to date
Imagination error follows a second-order power law in compute; downstream planning improves predictably with it
Checkpoints + training/robot-deployment code released; zero-shot goal-image planning on real hardware

stories.title: usamahz/cpu-performance-engineering
stories.reason: A primary-sources-only reading path for CPU performance engineering, ending in a dedicated inference-on-CPU section (GEMM/BLAS, quantization, AMX/SME, when CPUs beat GPUs) with 14 sections of runnable, fully-specified benchmarks (CPU model, core count, compiler flags required to quote a number) and an MCP server to query it — unusually rigorous for the 'how are models served' beat.
key_facts: 1102 GitHub stars, Python/C benchmarks, strict rule: a figure is dropped if it's missing CPU model/core count/compiler flags/baseline
Covers oneDNN, MLAS, ggml/llama.cpp kernels, int8/k-quant formats, NUMA-aware decode threading

stories.title: Sub-1-Bit LLM Compression via Latent Factorization
stories.reason: SamsungLabs' LittleBit pushes LLM weight compression below 1 bit/weight (down to 0.1 bpw) via low-rank latent factorization + binarization with a Joint-ITQ init, with training code released — the repo-attached exception that saves this from the arxiv-quantization-paper downvote pattern. No accuracy/perplexity numbers are actually published yet and pretrained weights look like a placeholder, so this is promising methodology, not a proven result.
key_facts: Targets 1.0 to 0.1 bits per weight via SVD latent factors binarized toward the hypercube
Code (single-GPU + DeepSpeed training, eval.py) released under CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial)
No accuracy/perplexity results published; HF weight repo referenced looks like a placeholder
